subject: Assessment trigger: custody, usage constraints, and return timeline
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Liu <emma@brightcart.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Assessment trigger: custody, usage constraints, and return timeline

Hi Emma —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. BrightCart’s ML infra and privacy constraints look like a good fit for a short evaluation with Redwood. To keep momentum, I want to put a very small mutual action plan (MAP) in place so we can exchange a limited promptpack and a sampling of testcases for your engineers to validate. High-level ask:

- We provide an ephemeral prompt pack (sample subset) + test-case CSV for acceptance testing.
- BrightCart agrees to scoped usage (sandbox-only, 30-day retention, no external redistribution).
- Legal sign-off (MPA) + security check completed in parallel.
- Close target: 3 weeks from acceptance to sandbox teardown unless extended by mutual agreement.

I attached a draft MAP outline and a small prompt/sample bundle we propose to share once we have the go-ahead. Can you confirm:
1) Who on your side will own the security questionnaire and legal review?
2) Any must-have restrictions beyond sandbox-only and destruction after 30 days?
3) Is the proposed 3-week close window workable?

If that aligns, I’ll share the limited asset bundle via our gated Drive link and include the acceptance gate checklist (basic functional pass + no PII exposure after run).

Thanks — looking forward to moving to the handoff step.

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: MAP_v1.pdf (outline), promptpack-sample.zip (subset), testcase-index.csv
From: Emma Liu <emma@brightcart.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: BrightCart Legal <legal@brightcart.com>
Date: 2026-08-12T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Assessment trigger: custody, usage constraints, and return timeline

Jordan —

Appreciate the clear plan. Quick answers:

1) Security questionnaire: I own the initial pass; legal will pick up contract/MPA redlines (cc'd).
2) Must-haves: sandbox-only, no production keys, no export of promptpack contents outside of our internal trial team (approx 6 engineers). Also prefer hashed testcases if possible (we can ingest salted hashes instead of raw user text).
3) 3-week close window looks fine, provided we can start this week and legal turnaround is ~5 business days.

Next steps from our side: I’ll run the questionnaire and return it by EOD 8/13. Legal (cc) will watch for the MAP and promptpack; please redact any customer-specific data before sharing.

Thanks — Emma
Emma Liu
Head of ML Platform
BrightCart

Emma —

Thanks for the quick reply. Attached is the MAP_v1.pdf (very short), a redacted promptpack-sample.zip (50 prompts, no customer PII), and the testcase-index.csv (hashes + expected labels). Key points in the MAP:

- Access lane: sandbox only (Redwood-hosted ephemeral tenant), 6 engineers allowed.
- Retention: 30 days from onboarding or 7 days post-close, whichever is later.
- Usage: evaluation only, no model training/derivatives for production.
- Escrow/escrow-equivalent: we keep the canonical assets; BrightCart may request a certified copy under a narrow NDA for audit purposes (we'll coordinate).
- Acceptance gate: functional pass on 500-run sample with <5% label drift on the seeded cases.

Please find the gated Drive link here: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/0BMAP/brightcart-onramp (access granted to your listed emails). I also uploaded the completed security questionnaire (security-questionnaire-completed.pdf) for your records.

Callouts for legal/security: note the no-derivatives clause and the destruction timeline. Happy to take any redlines but prefer to keep the MAP minimal so your engineering review can start immediately.

If we’re aligned I’ll mark a target close date: 2026-09-03 for sandbox teardown (3 weeks post-acceptance), with a mid-evaluation checkpoint on 8/24 to review results.

—Jordan

Attachments referenced: MAP_v1.pdf, promptpack-sample.zip, testcase-index.csv, security-questionnaire-completed.pdf
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-14T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: MAP & gated delivery: promptpack sample (redacted)

Fyi — forwarding the MAP and the attachments Emma will see. A couple of quick internal notes before we get into legal:

- Karthik: we should confirm whether the escrow-equivalent clause needs a separate MSA amendment or if MAP_v1 can act as an addendum. I lean toward addendum for speed.
- On retention: security asked we add a 2-step verification for anyone accessing the gated Drive; propose we require SSO + reviewer list. That should be acceptable and matches their ask of "internal trial team" only.
- On hashed testcases: ask the team if salted hashes are sufficient for their ingestion path; if not, propose an offset tokenization step in the sandbox.

Can you two draft a 1-paragraph clause for the MAP addendum covering: limited access, retention schedule, and no-derivatives? I’ll prep for legal.

—Lauren

Subject: Re: Assessment trigger: custody, usage constraints, and return timeline

Jordan / team —

We reviewed MAP_v1 and have one small redline request: replace the generic "destruction" language with a narrow verification process where BrightCart will certify destruction and Redwood will confirm by submitting MD5 checksums of destroyed assets (or an agreed attestation) within 3 business days of deletion. Also request a clause limiting number of internal recipients to the stated 6 and a requirement that BrightCart maintains an access log for the evaluation period.

We do not object to the 30-day retention window; we only ask that the retention clock starts on production of the final zipped asset in the gated Drive (not on first access).

If you can issue an updated MAP addendum with those two clarifications (destruction-attestation + access-log requirement + start-of-retention trigger), we can sign via DocuSign and proceed.

Best,
BrightCart Legal
legal@brightcart.com
